title: SN2: hydroxide + bromomethane
description: Concerted backside attack of hydroxide on bromomethane with loss of bromide; the C–H 'umbrella' inverts (Walden inversion).
reference: Clayden, Greeves & Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed., ch. 15

title: E2: ethoxide + 2-bromopropane
description: Ethoxide removes the β-hydrogen anti-periplanar to bromine while the C=C π bond forms and bromide leaves, all in one concerted step.
reference: Clayden, Greeves & Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed., ch. 17

title: Nucleophilic addition: cyanide + acetaldehyde
description: Cyanide attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of acetaldehyde; the C=O π electrons move onto oxygen to give a tetrahedral alkoxide (cyanohydrin anion).
reference: Clayden, Greeves & Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed., ch. 6

title: Electrophilic aromatic substitution: nitration, step 1
description: A benzene π bond attacks the nitronium ion to give the resonance-stabilised arenium (Wheland) intermediate; loss of H⁺ in the next step restores aromaticity.
reference: Clayden, Greeves & Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed., ch. 21

title: Diels–Alder: buta-1,3-diene + ethene
description: Concerted [4+2] cycloaddition: three π bonds are converted into two new σ bonds and one new π bond in a single cyclic, six-electron transition state.
reference: Clayden, Greeves & Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed., ch. 34

title: Radical homolysis: Cl₂ under light
description: Light (hν) cleaves the Cl–Cl bond homolytically; each chlorine atom keeps one electron of the bond (two fishhook arrows), giving two chlorine radicals.
reference: Clayden, Greeves & Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd ed., ch. 37

title: Lewis acid–base adduct: NH₃ + BF₃
description: The nitrogen lone pair of ammonia (Lewis base) is donated into the empty 2p orbital of boron trifluoride (Lewis acid), giving the adduct H₃N⁺–B⁻F₃.
reference: Housecroft & Sharpe, Inorganic Chemistry, 5th ed., ch. 'Acids, bases and ions in aqueous solution' (Lewis acids and bases)

title: Associative ligand substitution: [PtCl₄]²⁻ + NH₃
description: NH₃ adds to square-planar Pt(II) to give a five-coordinate (trigonal-bipyramidal) intermediate, which then loses Cl⁻ to give [PtCl₃(NH₃)]⁻. M–L bonds are drawn as single bonds with formal charges (Pt 2−/3−, coordinated N⁺).
reference: Housecroft & Sharpe, Inorganic Chemistry, 5th ed., ch. 'd-Block metal complexes: reaction mechanisms' (substitution in square planar complexes)

title: Hydrolysis of SiCl₄: attack of water at silicon
description: A water lone pair attacks silicon and chloride is displaced (drawn as one concerted, SN2-like step; the five-coordinate silicon species is not shown). Loss of H⁺ then gives Cl₃SiOH, and repetition gives Si(OH)₄/SiO₂.
reference: Housecroft & Sharpe, Inorganic Chemistry, 5th ed., ch. 'The group 14 elements' (halides of Si)

title: Brønsted acidity of a metal aqua ion: [Fe(OH₂)₆]³⁺ + H₂O
description: Polarisation by Fe(III) makes a coordinated water acidic: a solvent water removes a proton to give [Fe(OH₂)₅(OH)]²⁺ and H₃O⁺. M–L bonds are single bonds with formal charges (Fe 3−, aqua O⁺).
reference: Housecroft & Sharpe, Inorganic Chemistry, 5th ed., ch. 'Acids, bases and ions in aqueous solution' (aqua acids)

title: Serine protease acylation: catalytic triad attack on a peptide bond
description: His57, held by Asp102, acts as a general base and takes the Ser195 hydroxyl proton as the serine oxygen attacks the amide carbonyl, giving the tetrahedral oxyanion intermediate. Side chains are truncated (acetate, 4-methylimidazole, ethanol, N-methylacetamide).
reference: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed., ch. 9; Fersht, Structure and Mechanism in Protein Science (1999)

title: Alcohol dehydrogenase: hydride transfer to NAD⁺
description: The zinc-bound alkoxide of ethanol collapses to acetaldehyde while its C–H hydrogen is delivered as hydride to C4 of the nicotinamide ring (NAD⁺ modelled as 1-methylnicotinamide), giving the 1,4-dihydropyridine (NADH). Zn²⁺ is omitted.
reference: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed., ch. 16; Fersht, Structure and Mechanism in Protein Science (1999)

title: Kinase: in-line phosphoryl transfer from ATP
description: An active-site Asp acts as general base while the substrate hydroxyl attacks the γ-phosphorus in line with the β,γ-bridging oxygen, which leaves as ADP. ATP is modelled as methyl triphosphate, the substrate as ethanol; Mg²⁺ is omitted.
reference: Berg, Tymoczko, Gatto & Stryer, Biochemistry, 9th ed., ch. 9 (nucleoside monophosphate kinases); Fersht, Structure and Mechanism in Protein Science (1999)
